extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary text and figure captions; no placeholder automated mechanism context remains.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: L3 and L3-K are supported as membrane-active peptides in E. coli: cytological profiling plus PI/DiSC(3)5 assays indicate effects on both outer and inner membrane permeability/potential rather than rapid large-pore polymyxin-like disruption.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: L3 and L3-K in E. coli CCUG31246 and FhuA-overexpressing E. coli MC4100 model assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is membrane permeability/potential phenotype; the paper does not identify a molecular receptor or binding site.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C3 is supported as affecting E. coli membrane potential/permeability with a pattern closer to inner-membrane specificity than L3/L3-K in the source interpretation.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C3 in E. coli CCUG31246 and FhuA-overexpressing E. coli MC4100 model assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: C3 was weaker in Table 2 antimicrobial activity; mechanism evidence is phenotype-level membrane effect, not target identification.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Nucleoid relaxation/DNA compaction changes are source-supported phenotypes for C3, L3, and L3-K, but the paper treats them as possibly downstream of membrane interaction or translocation and does not prove direct nucleic-acid targeting.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C3, L3, and L3-K in E. coli cytological profiling
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote this to direct DNA-binding or nucleic-acid-target mechanism.
